subject: Mindspan: evidence for no-training/ownership + subprocessor inventory
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@mindspan.health>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@mindspan.health>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: operational proof of no-training + subprocessor list for DPA addendum

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week — Mindspan is excited about Redwood's latency and rollback policies. Before we can proceed with procurement we need a short evidence pack to satisfy our Legal and Privacy teams. Specifically: 

- An operations runbook or checklist that shows how you prevent customer data from being used for model improvement (no-training paths, toggle behavior, and KV/prefix cache retention).
- A current subprocessor inventory (hosting, telemetry, monitoring, any third-party tool that sees request/response data).
- Confirmation of data residency / cross-border transfer mechanics (we operate in EU and must ensure no unexpected transfers).
- Proposal language for response ownership and derivative rights we can insert into our DPA (we prefer a no-derivatives/no-train clause plus confirmation that prompt/response pairs are treated as tenant data).

Could you share a minimal package and suggested DPA redline? We aim to present to procurement on Friday (2026-08-13).

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Counsel, Mindspan Health

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@mindspan.health>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational proof of no-training + subprocessor list for DPA addendum

Elena — thank you, appreciate the clear list.

Kimberly (Privacy) and Marissa (Solutions/Onboarding) — looped you in to pull the evidence pack. High level answers for Mindspan's procurement timeline:

- We support a documented no-training operational mode for private and dedicated customers; hosted customers may choose opt-out. We have an Ops Runbook and an evidence checklist that shows how the toggle is enforced and how logs/telemetry are scoped.
- We'll attach the current subprocessor inventory and call out which subprocessors have access to persisted request/response data.
- For EU customers we can offer regional routing and onshore KMS options; I'll have Marissa confirm residencies and transfer controls.
- We'll propose DPA language that: 1) records Mindspan's exclusive ownership of prompts and responses, 2) prohibits Redwood from using the data for model improvement unless explicit written consent is given, and 3) outlines export controls for derivative artifacts.

I'll follow up with attachments and a suggested redline by EOD tomorrow. If Friday is the deadline, let's aim to have the redline + inventories to you by Thursday COB so you have a day to circulate.

— David
David Kim
Head of Trust & Security, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@mindspan.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Request: operational proof of no-training + subprocessor list for DPA addendum

Forwarding the attachments requested. See inline notes below.

--- Forwarded attachment list ---
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_no-train_addendum_v1.docx; subprocessor_inventory_aug2026.xlsx; ops_runbook_no-learn.pdf

Quick notes:
- ops_runbook_no-learn.pdf: shows the runtime toggle, KV cache eviction policy, and the audit trail for toggle changes (SOC2 control references included). It includes the step-by-step for responding to an internal audit and a sample run of a no-training mode verification script.
- subprocessor_inventory_aug2026.xlsx: column B flags whether the subprocessor receives persisted request/response content. We call out cloud hosting (eu-west-1), monitoring vendor, and a telemetry vendor used only for aggregated metrics (no PII).
- Redwood_DPA_no-train_addendum_v1.docx: suggested language for a DPA addendum — section titles: "No-Training Commitment", "Prompt and Response Ownership", "Derivative Restrictions and Escrow", and "Cross-border Routing and KMS Options".

Caveats: this is our proposed internal template; legal redlines are expected. For Mindspan's EU residency requirement we can lock routing to eu-west-1 and enable onshore KMS, but there are implementation windows for dedicated VPCs (we've documented expected lead times in the runbook).

Kimberly Park
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@mindspan.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@mindspan.health>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational proof of no-training + subprocessor list for DPA addendum

Kimberly — thank you, this is exactly the type of material our committee asked for. Quick clarifications before we circulate internally: 

1) The runbook mentions an audit script — can you provide the sample output (anonymized) so we can see what an audit report looks like?
2) On the subprocessor sheet, we need confirmation in writing that the telemetry vendor does not receive raw prompt/response pairs, and the monitoring vendor only sees aggregated metrics. Can you add a signed attestation line?
3) For the DPA addendum: Mindspan requires a firm "no-derivatives" line (not just no-training by policy) and an assurance that any derivative code or fine-tuned artifacts would be subject to escrow/escrow-only access under defined circumstances. Could you add proposed escrow language to the docx and highlight it?

If we can get the supplemental items by EOD Thursday that keeps us on track. Also, we'd prefer DocuSign for final signature.

Thanks again — will be in touch after procurement reviews.
Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@mindspan.health>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational proof of no-training + subprocessor list for DPA addendum

Elena — attaching two quick items inline here and uploading to the Drive link:

- sample_audit_output.txt (anonymized run of the verification script showing toggle state history, verification hashes, and retention windows)
- attestation_telemetry_signed.pdf (signed statement from our Product Ops lead confirming telemetry is aggregated and does not receive raw prompt/response pairs)

We also added a short escrow clause to the DPA addendum (last page) as a suggested starting point. If Mindspan wants stronger escrow controls we can expand that section.

Next steps from here: if the language looks OK to you, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet with the DPA addendum and a short SOW for onshore KMS + region lock. Estimated implementation lead time for dedicated onshore KMS: 6–8 weeks after signed SOW.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
